events.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor in Rome
events.description: On Christmas Day, Pope Leo III placed an imperial crown on Charlemagne in St. Peter's Basilica. He was proclaimed Emperor of the Romans before the gathered crowd.
events.significance: The coronation revived the idea of a western Roman Empire. It shaped the relationship between the papacy and European rulers for centuries.

events.title: William the Conqueror Crowned King of England
events.description: William, Duke of Normandy, was crowned king at Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day. This came just weeks after his victory at the Battle of Hastings.
events.significance: The Norman conquest transformed English government, language, land ownership and culture. Its effects are still visible in England today.

events.title: Washington Crosses the Delaware
events.description: On the night of Christmas Day, George Washington led Continental Army troops across the icy Delaware River. They were heading for a surprise attack on Hessian forces at Trenton, New Jersey, which came the next morning.
events.significance: The victory at Trenton lifted American morale at a low point in the Revolutionary War. It helped keep the fight for independence going.

events.title: Gorbachev Resigns and the Soviet Union Ends
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as Soviet president and handed over his powers. That evening the Soviet flag was lowered over the Kremlin for the last time and replaced by the Russian tricolor.
events.significance: The moment marked the end of the Soviet Union and the Cold War. It reshaped the world order.
